frame: Tail frame: +z forward (toward the cabin), +y up, +x toward the airplane's left. Origin on the floor under the forward cut. The tailcone skin is see-through.
note: anchor = where the label and fly-to point sit on the built-in trainer empennage (web/app/models/empennage.js). Paired items (rudder horns, rudder cables, pulleys, turnbuckles) are anchored on the left run.

parts.name: Horizontal stabilizer
parts.description: The fixed horizontal surface the elevator hangs on. Its skin, spar line, leading edge and attach points are checked for deterioration, distortion, evidence of failure and insecure attachment.

sources.section: Outer Wing Surfaces and Tail Section

parts.name: Elevator
parts.description: The movable pitch control surface behind the stabilizer, driven by the elevator cables through a horn. Checked for damage, secure attachment, correct installation and free, full operation.

parts.name: Elevator trim tab
parts.description: A small adjustable surface on the elevator's trailing edge that relieves control pressure. It is rigged much like the main surfaces and moved by the trim actuator's push rod.

parts.name: Vertical fin
parts.description: The fixed vertical surface the rudder hangs on. Same checks as the horizontal stabilizer: skin, spar line, leading edge and attach points.

sources.section: Outer Wing Surfaces and Tail Section

parts.name: Rudder
parts.description: The movable yaw control surface on the fin, driven by the left and right rudder cables through its horns. Checked for damage, secure attachment and free, full operation.

parts.name: Hinges
parts.description: The brackets and bolts the elevator and rudder pivot on. A loose or worn hinge is an insecure attachment and lets the surface move where it should not.

parts.name: Control horns
parts.description: Arms on the elevator and rudder where the cables attach. Pulling a cable on a horn moves the surface. Checked for cracks, security and properly safetied cable ends.

parts.name: Control cables
parts.description: Steel cables run from the cockpit controls to the horns: two for the elevator, two for the rudder. Broken wires are easy to see, but wear, corrosion and distortion are not, so the critical fatigue areas get a close look.

parts.name: Pulleys
parts.description: Pulleys guide the cables and change their direction; brackets on the structure hold them. Their sealed bearings need no further lubrication, but each pulley must turn smoothly and show no abnormal cable wear pattern.

parts.name: Turnbuckles
parts.description: A threaded barrel with two terminals, fitted in each cable to make small adjustments in length and tension. Once adjusted, a turnbuckle must be safetied.

parts.name: Trim actuator
parts.description: A jackscrew actuator in the tailcone that moves the trim tab through a push rod. Checked for security, wear and free, correct operation.
